The fix: on line 33, `len(items) != 2` was changed to `len(items) == 2`.

**The bug:** The condition was inverted. When the list had exactly 2 items (e.g., `[1, 2, 3]` has 3 items, which is `!= 2`), it was hitting the branch that only joins two items with "and". And when the list had exactly 2 items, it was falling through to the `else` branch that uses commas. This meant a 3-element list like `[1, 2, 3]` produced `"1 and 2"` instead of `"1, 2 and 3"`.
